about.title: Garden Grove Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Garden Grove is home to more than 175,000 people, and most of them will sit in a doctor's office, urgent care, or hospital somewhere in Orange County this year. Nearly every one of those visits goes the way it should. Occasionally it does not, and the harm that follows can reshape a family's life along Chapman Avenue or Brookhurst Street in a matter of days. California treats these cases differently from an ordinary injury claim. Under MICRA, you generally have one year from the date you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to file. A 90-day notice must be sent to each provider before a lawsuit begins. A qualified medical expert almost always has to review the records and confirm that care fell below the accepted standard, because a poor result by itself is not malpractice. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Garden Grove residents with an independent attorney who can read your chart, weigh the deadlines, and tell you honestly whether a claim exists.

whyChoose.title: Why Garden Grove Residents Use LawProactive for Malpractice Claims

items.title: MICRA's clock is shorter than most people assume
items.desc: One year from discovery, capped at three years from the injury, leaves little room for waiting. Getting an attorney involved early protects your right to file at all.

items.title: The 90-day notice and expert review get handled properly
items.desc: California requires written notice to each provider before suit and, in nearly every case, a qualified medical expert to support the claim. The attorney you are connected with manages both so a procedural misstep does not sink a valid case.

items.title: Free connection, contingency representation
items.desc: LawProactive charges nothing to connect you. The independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery, and MICRA's non-economic damages cap — which rises each year — is explained up front.

items.question: My surgery at an Orange County hospital had a bad outcome. Is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law asks whether the provider's care fell below what a reasonably careful professional would have done in the same situation, and whether that lapse caused your harm. Complications can occur even with proper care. A qualified medical expert reviewing your records is how an attorney tells the difference.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in Garden Grove?
items.answer: Under MICRA, generally one year from when you discovered or reasonably should have discovered the injury, and no more than three years from the date of the injury itself. Before filing, a 90-day notice of intent must be served on each provider. Because these rules interact, it is wise to speak with an attorney as soon as you suspect something went wrong.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: MICRA places a statutory cap on non-economic damages such as pain and suffering, and that cap increases every year under current law. Economic losses like medical bills and lost income are handled separately. An attorney can walk you through how the current figures apply to your specific situation without making promises about any outcome.
